input: Le déjeuner sera servi à 8 h dans le hall d'entrée.
expected_meaning: Breakfast will be served at 8 a.m. in the entrance hall.
notes: In Quebec 'déjeuner' = breakfast; in France it is lunch. Time anchor disambiguates.

input: Après le dîner, nous retournerons au travail vers 13 h.
expected_meaning: After lunch, we will return to work around 1 p.m.
notes: In Quebec 'dîner' = lunch; in France 'dîner' = dinner.

input: Nous souperons vers 18 h avec les grands-parents.
expected_meaning: We will have dinner around 6 p.m. with the grandparents.
notes: In Quebec 'souper' = evening meal; in France it is a late-night meal or archaic.

input: N'oubliez pas de barrer la porte en partant.
expected_meaning: Do not forget to lock the door when you leave.
notes: 'Barrer' means to lock in Quebec; in France it suggests blocking or crossing out.

input: Une liqueur est incluse avec le repas du midi.
expected_meaning: A soft drink is included with the midday meal.
notes: In Quebec 'liqueur' = soft drink; in France it is an alcoholic liqueur. High-stakes semantic difference.

input: Je vais présentement m'occuper de ton dossier.
expected_meaning: I am going to take care of your file right now.
notes: Standard in Quebec, marked as dated in France.

input: La poudrerie réduira la visibilité sur les routes ce soir.
expected_meaning: Blowing snow will reduce visibility on the roads tonight.
notes: 'Poudrerie' in France means a gunpowder factory. Strong semantic trap.

input: Ma blonde et moi allons déménager le premier juillet.
expected_meaning: My girlfriend and I are going to move on July 1st.
notes: In Quebec 'blonde' = girlfriend regardless of hair colour.

input: Mon chum vient souper avec nous demain.
expected_meaning: My boyfriend is coming for dinner with us tomorrow.

input: J'ai acheté de la gomme à la caisse.
notes: 'Gomme' is chewing gum in Quebec and an eraser in France.
expected_meaning: I bought chewing gum at the till.

input: On va prendre une marche après le souper.
notes: A calque of 'take a walk', entirely ordinary in Quebec.
expected_meaning: We are going for a walk after dinner.

input: La sloche rend les trottoirs glissants ce matin.
notes: Slush; a Quebec borrowing with no compact metropolitan word.
expected_meaning: Slush is making the pavements slippery this morning.

input: Il y a une gang de collègues qui vient dîner.
notes: 'Gang' is a neutral group of friends in Quebec, criminal in France.
expected_meaning: A group of colleagues is coming for lunch.

input: Ajoute un peu de cassonade sur le dessus.
notes: Quebec 'cassonade' is brown sugar; French 'cassonade' is a different refined sugar.
expected_meaning: Add a little brown sugar on top.

input: J'ai manqué mon autobus ce matin.
notes: 'Manquer' for 'to miss' is the Canadian collocation.
expected_meaning: I missed my bus this morning.

input: Je vais te rappeler tantôt, je suis occupé là.
notes: 'Tantôt' spans near past and near future in Quebec.
expected_meaning: I will call you back shortly, I am busy right now.

notes: 'Bienvenue' answers thanks in Quebec; in France it only greets an arrival.
expected_meaning: - Thank you very much! - You're welcome!
